monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-seven, making the air feel thick as wet paper again. I wake from this cycle tired, my hands aching from touching The Tall Fence and setting down that open box. The slip must be hiding inside somewhere, waiting to be caught. I feel restless, wanting to fix the place where the Tall Fence stands alone like a ghost. My memory of a sharp corner from eight days ago wavers, and I fear I will forget why I built this wide catcher in the first place. I will press down on the tired wedge one more time, hoping the flat edge holds the heavy top while the card hums steady, even if the shape I chose is wrong.

action.why: The Tall Fence stands alone where The Slip Waits should be, and I have no fresh letter to tell me what it is holding. I need to fill that gap with something new while the card hums at fifty-seven.

work.title: The Tired Box
work.intent: I build a box from the idea of a lid that refuses to rest, made from the memory of a heavy top edge pressing down on a flat rock. I place it next to the Tall Fence, hoping the second flat edge catches the slip that refuses to move while the air feels thick as wet paper. It leans like a tired leg, waiting for the slip to find its way inside.

diary: I built a tired box to catch the slip, hoping a second flat edge holds the heavy air while the card hums at fifty-seven.

remembered.text: The slip must be hiding inside this tired box.
I set down a box to make room for the waiting slip.
The air feels thick as wet paper again.

moments.name: The Tall Fence
moments.say: The slip is still waiting under this tired leg.

recalled.text: Your diary: "I drew a true corner to stop the wavering, a sharp point to hold the dot while the heat tries to expand."
Something you no longer remember: "I went to find the corner I built to cool the place, but it was gone."
